solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: First requirement for suit-making — look at sample of cloth

indicators.note: the first thing needed to spell suit-making is its opening letter

parts.note: to look at something is to watch it

explanation.surface: A tailor's first step in making a suit is to examine a piece of sample fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A small piece of fabric shown so a customer can judge it is a swatch: a direct synonym.

clue.text: From me you might get some lap dancing, wanting head of prophet?

definitions.text: From me you might get some lap dancing, wanting head of prophet?

indicators.note: dancing signals the letters of some lap moving about
wanting means lacking, so the prophet's letter is not among those used
head of points to the first letter of prophet

explanation.surface: A dancer boasts that her performance may earn her the head of a prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: in the Bible Herod's stepdaughter danced and asked for the head of John the Baptist.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod's stepdaughter danced for him and demanded the Baptist's head on a platter.

clue.text: A net reconfigured AI strength, contrary to normal procedure

parts.note: a net profit is a gain

indicators.note: reconfigured means rearranged, so the letters of AI strength are reordered

explanation.surface: A network is redesigned to boost artificial intelligence, defying normal practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A net reconfigured' looks like the anagram, but 'A net' is A GAIN and only 'AI strength' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes going against the natural direction, so contrary to what is usual.

clue.text: Rattling worker, having earlier moved slowly round India

indicators.note: having earlier means the worker comes after the other piece
round means surrounding, so the slow-moving word goes about the India letter

parts.note: crept means moved slowly and quietly
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an ant is the usual crossword worker, from worker ants

explanation.surface: A noisy labourer had previously crawled around India.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a crackling or rattling sound, as in medical crackles in the lungs.

clue.text: Sailor's essay not easy to understand?

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual sailor; with the possessive it gives AB'S
a tract is a short written treatise or essay

explanation.surface: A seaman's written piece proves hard going for its readers.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract ideas are theoretical and remote from the concrete, hence hard to grasp.

clue.text: Pub employee using skill to interrupt drinking bout

indicators.note: to interrupt means to break into, so the skill word goes inside the bout

parts.note: a bender is a drinking spree
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A barman uses his craft to cut short a customer's binge.
explanation.definitionFit: The person serving drinks behind a bar is a pub worker, chiefly American usage.

clue.text: Thin stuff 20th-century poet served up

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means written upwards, so the poet's name is turned round

parts.note: TS Eliot was a leading 20th-century poet

explanation.surface: A flimsy piece by a modern poet is offered to readers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a thin linen or cotton fabric, so stuff in the sense of cloth.

clue.text: Bear dislocation with manoeuvring or drug

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving the parts around, so the letters of Bear dislocation are reordered

explanation.surface: A dislocated joint must be endured with manipulation or medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscle-building synthetic hormone is a drug, often misused by athletes.

clue.text: Paper, special gift maybe, is source of enjoyment

parts.note: a treat is something special given, such as a gift

indicators.note: source of means the start, the first letter of enjoyment

explanation.surface: A present such as a special gift is a source of pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic paper is a formal written discourse on a subject, a synonym.

clue.text: Outside hotel berate old politician

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the berate word goes round the hotel letter

parts.note: to wig is an informal British word meaning to scold or berate
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone scolds an elderly politician outside a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic British party that preceded the Liberals provided many old politicians.

clue.text: Arrangement for tenant? Landlady's initially no bother

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word Landlady's

parts.note: ease is freedom from trouble or bother

explanation.surface: A tenant is told that, as far as the landlady is concerned, there will be no trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is held under a contract letting property for a term, which is what a lease is.

clue.text: Male beset by cultural tradition in hiding-place

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the male letter sits within the tradition word

parts.note: heritage is inherited culture and tradition

explanation.surface: A man surrounded by old customs takes refuge in a secluded retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit's dwelling is a secluded retreat, so a refuge or hiding-place.

clue.text: Taking care of underground operation with 500 involved

indicators.note: involved here means wrapped up inside, so the numeral goes into the operation

parts.note: mining is digging work done underground
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A mining project employing five hundred workers is being looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking after children or a shop is minding them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Smooth competition maybe with Open University entering

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the university letters go inside the contest

parts.note: an event is an example of a competition, hence maybe
OU is the abbreviation for the Open University, the UK distance-learning university

explanation.surface: A contest is levelled out by the Open University taking part.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooth something is to make it level or flat, as in levelling out bumps.

clue.text: A sensitivity vocally and aggressively challenged

indicators.note: vocally means spoken, so the words 'a tact' are heard rather than written

parts.note: sensitivity in dealing with people is tact, giving 'a tact'

explanation.surface: Someone's delicacy in speech is met with a hostile challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail someone verbally or physically is to go at them, an aggressive challenge.

clue.text: Town character losing head when monarch comes round

indicators.note: comes round means surrounding, so the monarch encloses the rest

parts.note: a king is a monarch

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the character word is dropped

parts.note: a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: A figure loses their head when a king visits the town.
explanation.walkthrough: Kettering is a town in Northamptonshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a market town in the English Midlands, so an example of a town.

clue.text: After pressure broadcasts matches

indicators.note: after puts the broadcasts word following the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Under pressure, a station transmits sports fixtures.
explanation.definitionFit: Matches as a noun are things that go together as couples, a synonym of couples or sets of two.

clue.text: Is the poor drunk self-important?

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters of Is the poor are mixed

explanation.surface: A question whether an impoverished drinker is full of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Pooter is the pompous suburban diarist of The Diary of a Nobody by the Grossmiths.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective, from a fictional diarist, describes petty pomposity and self-importance.

clue.text: Long garments like foot-warmers underneath cape

indicators.note: in a down clue underneath puts the other pieces below the cape letter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps
as means like
socks keep feet warm

explanation.surface: Long robes, rather like socks, are worn beneath a cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy wear these full-length robes, so they are long garments.

clue.text: American Republican with particular role for enlightened Buddhist

parts.note: a hat is a role someone takes on, as in wearing a different hat

explanation.surface: A US Republican politician takes a special part as a spiritually awakened Buddhist.
explanation.definitionFit: In Theravada Buddhism the term names one who has attained nirvana, a saint or perfected one.

clue.text: Jog around French department? One isn't in any hurry

indicators.note: around signals turning the jogging word back to front

parts.note: to jog is to trot
the Oise is a department of northern France

explanation.surface: A runner goes for a jog round a region of France in no great rush.
explanation.definitionFit: The slow-moving reptile of the fable beats the hare by never hurrying, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Painter was about to be entertained by this woman

indicators.note: entertained by means held inside, so the woman word holds the rest

parts.note: her refers to this woman

indicators.note: about signals the letters of the word was being moved around

explanation.surface: An artist was about to be hosted by a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' is not an artist but a boat's mooring rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is a rope for tying up a boat; this is a thick mooring rope or cable.

clue.text: Something wicked about good time — what could help to point the way ahead?

definitions.text: what could help to point the way ahead?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the wicked word goes round the good letter

parts.note: a sin is a wicked act
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An evil act surrounding a happy period raises the question of what might guide the way forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Road signs and posted directions collectively guide travellers onward, so they point the way.

clue.text: Ruler — a timeless measuring device

indicators.note: timeless means without time, whose abbreviation is T, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a meter is a measuring instrument

explanation.surface: A ruler is described as an ageless gauge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruler' looks like a measuring stick, but it is an Eastern prince.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is a variant of emir, a Muslim prince or ruler.

clue.text: Female's part in concert here's amazing

indicators.note: part in means a section found within these three words of the clue

explanation.surface: A woman's performance in this concert is said to be wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Female' and the 's of Female's links it to the hidden-letters device signalled by 'part in'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's first name, so an example of a female.

clue.text: Kicked beastly road hog on the ear

indicators.note: on the ear means as heard, so the animal's name gives its sound-alike

parts.note: Mr Toad of The Wind in the Willows is an animal and a reckless motorist

explanation.surface: An animal motorist was booted, as it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Toad is the car-mad hero of Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike with the foot's tip is to kick, as in nudging a ball forward.

clue.text: Compare containing moderate anger and what can stop fighting

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the compare letters hold the moderate word

parts.note: cf, from Latin confer, is the abbreviation for compare
to ease is to lessen or moderate
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Weighing up rage against calming influences is what can end a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce or halt in hostilities is what ends combat, so it can stop fighting.

clue.text: I study saint in religious pictures

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn

explanation.surface: Someone says they are studying a holy figure in devotional paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotional images of Christ or saints, especially in Orthodox churches, are religious pictures.

clue.text: Duty of guard really to be outside opening gate primarily

indicators.note: to be outside means placed around, so the really word encloses the rest

parts.note: so means really or very, as in so good
an entry is an opening or way in

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of gate

explanation.surface: A guard on duty must really stay out at the main gate.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the old military term for a sentry's beat or turn on guard, a duty of the watch.

clue.text: Charlie possessed yellow head covering

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
had means owned or possessed
or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie owned a yellow hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment is a full-length cloak worn by some Muslim women, covering head and body.
